To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) the SNR variability of the network analysis is a useful indicator of the accuracy of the sky location estimate and (ii) the SNR penalty method is an effective means to suppress large variability of the network SNR.

the network analysis of a gravitational wave burst signal is improved by the introduction of a penalty term in the likelihood functional, which is proportional to the SNR variability of candidate waveforms as they are displaced on the sky; and that the method can be applied irrespective of the number of detectors in the network.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the detection of gravitational waves from compact binary coalescence, and the estimation of the source parameters.
the analysis of gravitational wave bursts from a network of gravitational wave interferometers.
the development of new statistical methods that will enable the detection and estimation of the source of gravitational wave bursts with a high degree of confidence.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
, if the source is a burst, then the signal is not a burst.
, for a network of two non-orthogonal detectors, the likelihood method is more efficient than the matched-filter method in the sense that it gives a more accurate estimate of the source position.

the network analysis of burst data with a priori polarization waveforms is a difficult problem, and that the use of the penalty functional can improve the estimation of sky position and waveform parameters.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have developed a network analysis technique which is more efficient in the sense that it can detect sources more easily, and estimate source properties more precisely.
the penalty functional can be used as a diagnostic tool to assess whether the network is well-conditioned for a given source position.
this method can be used to detect and localize gravitational wave burst signals with an arbitrary number of detectors.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the SNR of gravitational wave burst sources can be significantly variable over the sky, even in the case of a well-aligned network of detectors, and that this variability can lead to significant errors in estimation if not accounted for in analysis methods.
the SNR variability of a network of detectors can be used to suppress ill-conditioned solutions and improve the network analysis of burst signals.
the network analysis of burst signals should be performed using a likelihood procedure with a penalty for SNR variability.
